items.title: pre-fight-help-not-visible
items.claim: The qualifier card in Image #2 shows FIGHT and both sticks, but neither the Techniques nor Settings control visible in Image #3.
items.reason: A new player needs access to instructions and accessibility options before starting the fight.
items.suggest: Expose the existing Techniques and Settings actions on the qualifier card alongside FIGHT.

items.title: stick-actions-separated-from-controls
items.claim: In Image #3, the stick rims contain only directional chevrons, while their action mappings appear in a separate strip above them.
items.reason: The player must translate between the legend and the thumb position rather than read the action at its input location.
items.suggest: Replace the rim chevrons with the corresponding action labels, preserving the centered stick position and an 18 CSS px text minimum.

items.title: desktop-key-legend-absent
items.claim: Image #9 shows STANCE and TECHNIQUE beneath the desktop sticks without any visible keyboard key mappings.
items.reason: The displayed controls do not tell a keyboard player which keys to use.
items.suggest: Show the actual configured stance and technique keys in the unused space between the desktop sticks.

items.title: briefing-copy-all-caps
items.claim: Image #2 renders both the opponent briefing and the multi-line move instruction in widely spaced uppercase text.
items.reason: The explanatory copy competes with the round heading instead of providing an easily scanned introduction.
items.suggest: Keep the heading uppercase, but render the briefing and instructions in sentence case with left alignment and normal letter spacing.

items.title: kick-silhouette-unresolved
items.claim: Images #13 and #22 both display FRONT KICK, but the lifted foot is not clearly separable in #13 as it is in #22; this difference alone does not establish sprite clipping.
items.reason: A readable attack silhouette matters, but a normal pose or foreshortened limb must not be mistaken for missing artwork.
items.suggest: Make no sprite correction yet; capture the exact pose identifier and atlas rectangle for #13, then compare the rendered silhouette with the source cell's alpha bounds and consecutive frames.
